limitations: The evidence settles the narrower customer-price proposition but not the combined provider-and-customer cost assertion.
No numerical meaning can be assigned to calamitously expensive from the text alone.

statement.excerpt: AI is calamitously expensive and, despite years of promises of it getting cheaper for both those running AI services and its customers, costs have only ever increased.

from_speaker: for both those running AI services and its customers
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading of getting cheaper includes the cost of buying a comparable amount of service.
The word only makes the historical assertion categorical: a genuine comparable price reduction would defeat its customer unit-price component.
The historical period ends on publication. No starting date is supplied, so none is invented.
Total spending, prices per token and providers' production costs are separate measures.
No accounting basis is indicated. The supplied money rule therefore prevents a supported or contradicted score for the bundled financial claim.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable historical records would need to show that neither customer service costs nor provider operating costs ever declined within the claimed history, using consistently defined measures.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented reduction in the price of a comparable service would contradict the customer unit-price reading. A documented comparable provider cost reduction would contradict the provider component. Decisive financial scoring additionally requires a matching accounting basis.
